Let me analyze this OIML certificate for water meters.

Certificate details:
- Number: R49/2013-A-CZ1-2021.07, Revision 2
- Scheme: A
- Member State: Czech Republic
- Issuing Authority: Czech Metrology Institute, Okružní 31, 638 00 Brno, Czech Republic
- Person responsible: Jan Kalandra
- Applicant: George Kent (Malaysia) Berhad, Lot 1115, Jalan Puchong, Taman Meranti Jaya, 47120 Puchong, Selangor, Malaysia
- Manufacturer: same
- Certified type: water meter – positive displacement, dry dial; GKMV40, GKMV40P
- Module designation: "-" → "Not applicable"
- Recommendation: OIML R 49, Edition 2013
- Accuracy class: 2
- Date issued: 19 September 2023 (date on signature page)
- Page total: 9
- Project number: 0511? The reports have numbers like 0511-ER-V41-23. The project number could be "0511". Hmm, the schema asks for project_number if present. There's no explicit "project number" field. I'll omit or use 0511? Better to omit since not explicitly present. Actually the test report numbers begin with 0511 — that's CMI's internal project. I'll omit project_number since not explicitly stated.

oiml_issuer_id: not present. Omit.

Issuing authority person responsible on page 2: RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body. Person responsible on page 1: Jan Kalandra. The schema has person_responsible and person_title. On page 1, "Person responsible: Jan Kalandra". Page 2 signature: RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body. I'll use Jan Kalandra as person_responsible (as labeled), and maybe include Pavel Klenovský... The schema only has one person_responsible/person_title. Hmm. Page 1 explicitly says "Person responsible: Jan Kalandra". I'll use that. But person_title isn't given for him. The signed by is Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body. I could set person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra" and omit person_title. Alternatively use Klenovský with title "Head of Certification Body". The label "Person responsible" is explicit, so Jan Kalandra. I'll add nothing for title. Actually, maybe I can note both. The schema fields are person_responsible, person_title. I'll go with Jan Kalandra (explicit label). 

Date issued: 19 September 2023 → "2023-09-19".

Test reports:
1. OIML type evaluation report No. 0511-ER-V41-23 dated 10 August 2023, 33 pages including annex 1 → role: type_evaluation_report
2. Test report No. 6015-PT-P5008-23 issued by CMI dated 9 August 2023, 26 pages including annexes → role: test_report
3. OIML type evaluation report No. 0511-ER-V056-22 dated 27 September 2022, 29 pages → type_evaluation_report
4. OIML type evaluation report No. 0511-ER-V114-21 dated 22 October 2021, 90 pages → type_evaluation_report
5. Test report No. 6015-PT-P5009-21 issued by CMI dated 30 November 2021, 67 pages → test_report

Documentation file: 0511-UL-V041-23 → documentation_file

Revision history:
- "-" (initial), 6 December 2021, Issuing certificate → revision "0"? The table says "-" for revision number. Schema says revision string e.g. "0" not 0. The original had "-". Hmm. For initial issue, the convention is revision 0. The markdown literally has "-". I could use "0" as canonical, but "don't fabricate"... The instruction example says revision (string, e.g. "0" not 0). The table shows "-" for the initial. I think using "0" is reasonable canonicalization but it could be seen as fabrication. Let me keep it as "0" since "-" denotes no revision i.e., original. Actually, safer: use "0"? Hmm. Many previous examples use "0" for the issuing entry. I'll use "0".
- Revision 1, 8 August 2022, Added sizes DN20, DN25 and GKMV40-Sensors and Sealing
- Revision 2, 19 September 2023, Added sizes DN32 and DN40 GKMV40

Footnotes:
1) "Valid for water meter with an electronic device; if it is equipped, these classes are set in combination with parameters of ancillary device. Information specified by the manufacturer."
2) "Ancillary devices – reed sensor and inductive sensor – have not been tested."

Model family: The cert covers models GKMV40 and GKMV40P, each in sizes DN15, DN20, DN25 (both types) and DN32, DN40 (GKMV40 only). Wait — the first table covers GKMV40, GKMV40P with nominal diameters 15, 20, 25. The second table covers GKMV40 only with nominal diameters 32, 40.

Revision 1 added DN20, DN25; Revision 2 added DN32, DN40. Original was DN15.

So models: 
- GKMV40 DN15, GKMV40 DN20, GKMV40 DN25, GKMV40 DN32, GKMV40 DN40, GKMV40P DN15, GKMV40P DN20, GKMV40P DN25.

Model IDs: "GKMV40-DN15", "GKMV40-DN20", "GKMV40-DN25", "GKMV40-DN32", "GKMV40-DN40", "GKMV40P-DN15", "GKMV40P-DN20", "GKMV40P-DN25".

Model-level characteristics from the tables:

Table 1 (GKMV40 & GKMV40P, DN15/20/25):
- Q1: 0.0063, 0.01, 0.0158 m³/h
- Q2: 0.0100, 0.016, 0.0252 m³/h
- Q3: 2.50, 4.0, 6.30 m³/h
- Q4: 3.13, 5.0, 7.88 m³/h
- Q3/Q1: 400 (all)
- Q2/Q1: 1.6
- Q3/Q4: 1.25
- Measuring principle: positive displacement
- Accuracy class: 2
- MPE lower zone: ±5%
- MPE upper zone: ±2% ≤30°C; ±3% >30°C
- Temperature class: T30 or T50
- Water pressure class: MAP 16
- Pressure loss class: ΔP 63
- Environmental class: B, O (footnote 1)
- Electromagnetic environment: E1 (footnote 1)
- Mechanical class: M1 (footnote 1)
- Max admissible temperature: 50 °C
- Max admissible pressure: 1.6 MPa
- Orientation limitation: any
- Indicating range [m³]: DN15: "9999 or 99 999"; DN20: 99999; DN25: 99999
- Resolution of indicating device [m³]: DN15: "0.000002 or 0.00002"; DN20: 0.00002; DN25: 0.00002
- Resolution of device for rapid testing [dm³]: 156.6, 89.7, 47.49
- EUT category: Positive displacement water meters; Case: A
- Connection type: DN15: G¾”B x G¾”B / G⅞”B x G¾”B; DN20: G1”B / W36.6x14TPI / W32.5x14TPI; DN25: G1¼”B
- Min straight length inlet: 0 mm; outlet: 0 mm
- Flow conditioner: No
- Mounting: in line meter
- Orientation: any
- Body: brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P)
- Length [mm]: DN15: 110; 115; 134; 165; 190; DN20: 154; 165; DN25: 199; 260
- Reed sensor power supply (Umax/Imax): max 48 V DC/AC / 50 mA (footnote 2)
- Inductive sensor power supply: max 24 V DC / 20 mA (footnote 2)

Table 2 (GKMV40 only, DN32/40):
- Q1: 0.025, 0.040
- Q2: 0.040, 0.064
- Q3: 10.0, 16.0
- Q4: 12.5, 20.0
- Q3/Q1: 400
- Q2/Q1: 1.6
- Q3/Q4: 1.25
- Same classes...
- Indicating range: 99 999 both
- Resolution: 0.00002 both
- Rapid testing resolution: 31.05, 15.066 dm³
- Connection: DN32: G1½"B / G1¾"B; DN40: G2B
- Length: DN32: 260; DN40: 225; 300
- Same sensor power supply values.

Now build model_level entries. Attributes varying by model:

- nominal_diameter_mm: 15, 20, 25, 32, 40 (per model). Actually the nominal diameter is part of the model id (DN). I can include it anyway.
- q1 (m³/h): per size, same for GKMV40 and GKMV40P.
- q2, q3, q4 similarly.
- indicating_range_m3: DN15 variants: "9999 or 99999" (string), others 99999.
- resolution_indicating_device_m3: DN15: "0.000002 or 0.00002", others 0.00002.
- resolution_rapid_testing_device_dm3: 156.6, 89.7, 47.49, 31.05, 15.066 per size.
- connection_type: per size (string list).
- length_mm: lists per size: DN15: [110,115,134,165,190]; DN20: [154,165]; DN25: [199,260]; DN32: [260]; DN40: [225,300].
- body_material: brass for GKMV40, composite for GKMV40P.

Type-level characteristics:
- ratio_q3_q1: 400
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6
- ratio_q3_q4: 1.25
- measuring_principle: positive displacement
- accuracy_class: 2
- mpe_lower_flowrate_zone: ±5% → value -5 to 5? Better: value: 5, unit: "%", or string "±5%". Rule says numbers not strings. ±5% could be {min:-5, max:5}. Hmm. For MPE it's a limit. I'll use value: 5, unit_symbol: "%", with label "maximum_permissible_error_lower_zone". Or min/max. I'll use {min: -5, max: 5}? That might misrepresent. The MPE is ±5%, meaning error within ±5%. {min:-5,max:5} is accurate. For upper zone, ±2% ≤30°C and ±3% >30°C — that's config-level by temperature. I'll do config_level entries:
  - attribute: maximum_permissible_error_upper_zone, axis: water_temperature, values: [{condition: "≤30°C", value: ±2%}, {condition: ">30°C", value: ±3%}]. Structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. value: {min:-2,max:2}, unit "%". 

- temperature_class: "T30 or T50" → string value. Maybe list ["T30","T50"]. I'll keep string "T30 or T50".
- water_pressure_class: "MAP 16"
- pressure_loss_class: "ΔP 63" → canonical label pressure_loss_class, value "ΔP 63" (avoid LaTeX; Δ is fine as Unicode). 
- environmental_class: "B, O" footnote 1
- electromagnetic_environment: "E1" footnote 1
- mechanical_class: "M1" footnote 1
- maximum_admissible_temperature: 50 °C
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa
- orientation_limitation: any
- eut_test_category: Positive displacement water meters
- eut_test_case: A
- min_straight_length_inlet_pipe: 0 mm
- min_straight_length_outlet_pipe: 0 mm
- flow_conditioner: No
- mounting: in line meter
- orientation: any
- reed_sensor_power_supply: Umax 48 V DC/AC, Imax 50 mA. Split into: reed_sensor_max_voltage: 48 V; reed_sensor_max_current: 50 mA; reed_sensor_voltage_type: "DC/AC". footnote 2.
- inductive_sensor_max_voltage: 24 V DC; inductive_sensor_max_current: 20 mA. footnote 2.

Matrix table: preserve the type-details tables as matrix_tables? The schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The flow characteristics fit model_level. But I could also add a matrix_table for the flow data by size. The R137 example populates both matrix_tables AND model_level. I'll add matrix_tables for the two tables (DN15-25 and DN32-40), plus maybe installation details. Keep it manageable: one matrix table "Flow characteristics by nominal diameter" covering all 5 sizes with columns: nominal_diameter, q1, q2, q3, q4. And maybe another for installation details (connection type, lengths). I'll do two matrix tables:

1. "Type details by nominal diameter (GKMV40 and GKMV40P)" — rows per size: DN15, DN20, DN25, DN32, DN40 with q1, q2, q3, q4, indicating_range, resolution, rapid_testing_resolution, lengths, connection.

Actually GKMV40P only exists for DN15-25. The first table covers both types; second only GKMV40. I'll make matrix table rows with nominal_diameter and the values; description notes applicability.

Let me design:

matrix_tables:
[
  {
    name: "Basic technical data by nominal diameter",
    columns: ["nominal_diameter", "q1", "q2", "q3", "q4", "indicating_range", "resolution_indicating_device", "resolution_rapid_testing"],
    column_units: [null, "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³", "m³", "dm³"],
    rows: [
      {nominal_diameter: 15, q1: 0.0063, q2: 0.0100, q3: 2.50, q4: 3.13, indicating_range: "9999 or 99 999", resolution_indicating_device: "0.000002 or 0.00002", resolution_rapid_testing: 156.6},
      {nominal_diameter: 20, q1: 0.01, q2: 0.016, q3: 4.0, q4: 5.0, indicating_range: 99999, resolution_indicating_device: 0.00002, resolution_rapid_testing: 89.7},
      {nominal_diameter: 25, q1: 0.0158, q2: 0.0252, q3: 6.30, q4: 7.88, indicating_range: 99999, resolution_indicating_device: 0.00002, resolution_rapid_testing: 47.49},
      {nominal_diameter: 32, q1: 0.025, q2: 0.040, q3: 10.0, q4: 12.5, indicating_range: 99999, resolution_indicating_device: 0.00002, resolution_rapid_testing: 31.05},
      {nominal_diameter: 40, q1: 0.040, q2: 0.064, q3: 16.0, q4: 20.0, indicating_range: 99999, resolution_indicating_device: 0.00002, resolution_rapid_testing: 15.066}
    ],
    description: "First table applies to types GKMV40 and GKMV40P (DN15–DN25); DN32 and DN40 apply to type GKMV40 only.",
    footnotes: []
  },
  {
    name: "Installation details by nominal diameter",
    columns: ["nominal_diameter", "connection_type", "length"],
    rows: [
      {nominal_diameter: 15, connection_type: ["G¾”B x G¾”B", "G⅞”B x G¾”B"], length: [110, 115, 134, 165, 190]},
      ...
    ]
  }
]

Hmm, schema rows is "object per row" — arrays within objects are fine.

Components: The cert mentions ancillary devices: reed sensor and inductive sensor (not tested). Also indicating device. The schema says include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The reed sensor/inductive sensor are ancillary devices with power supply limits. I could add components:
- role: "ancillary_device", type_designations: ["reed sensor", "inductive sensor"]... alternatives "OR"? They're options. I'll include a components entry: role "ancillary device (pulser)", type_designations ["Reed impulse transmitter", "Inductive transmitter"], characteristics with power supply limits. Hmm — is this over-extraction? The cert does name them as ancillary devices. I'll include one components entry with alternatives "OR" between reed and inductive sensors. Characteristics: max voltage/current.

Actually, maybe simpler: include components for the indicating device? Not really named as separate type. I'll include the ancillary devices component since it has test status notes.

certified_type:
- category: "Water meter" (schema example says "Gas meter", "Measuring system"... "Water meter" fits).
- type_designations: ["GKMV40", "GKMV40P"]
- module_designation: "Not applicable" (the field shows "-")
- description: "Positive displacement water meter with dry mechanical indicating device..." 

Recommendation: id "R49", edition 2013, scheme "A", accuracy_classes [2].

certificate:
- number: "R49/2013-A-CZ1-2021.07"
- scheme: "A"
- project_number: not present — omit.
- page_total: 9
- member_state: "Czech Republic"
- date_issued: "2023-09-19"
- oiml_issuer_id: omit

Revision history: also revision on certificate is "Revision 2". revision_history entries:
- {revision: "0", date: "2021-12-06", changes: "Issuing certificate"}
- {revision: "1", date: "2022-08-08", changes: "Added sizes DN20, DN25 and GKMV40-Sensors and Sealing"}
- {revision: "2", date: "2023-09-19", changes: "Added sizes DN32 and DN40 GKMV40"}

model_family:
- family_name: "GKMV40" — the family name could be "GKMV40 / GKMV40P". I'll set family_name: "GKMV40" and note P variant. Hmm, GKMV40P is a separate type designation. family_name: null? The cert doesn't give an explicit family name. I'll use null and list models.

models: 8 entries:
- GKMV40-DN15, GKMV40-DN20, GKMV40-DN25, GKMV40-DN32, GKMV40-DN40, GKMV40P-DN15, GKMV40P-DN20, GKMV40P-DN25
With attributes: body_material, nominal_diameter_mm.

model_level characteristics:
1. nominal_diameter — values per model (or type-level? varies by model → model_level).
2. q1 m³/h: DN15 0.0063; DN20 0.01; DN25 0.0158; DN32 0.025; DN40 0.04 (same for GKMV40 and GKMV40P).
3. q2: 0.0100, 0.016, 0.0252, 0.040, 0.064
4. q3: 2.50, 4.0, 6.30, 10.0, 16.0
5. q4: 3.13, 5.0, 7.88, 12.5, 20.0
6. indicating_range m³: DN15 models: "9999 or 99 999" (string, since two options); others 99999.
7. resolution_indicating_device m³: DN15: "0.000002 or 0.00002"; others 0.00002.
8. resolution_rapid_testing_device dm³: 156.6 (DN15), 89.7 (DN20), 47.49 (DN25), 31.05 (DN32), 15.066 (DN40).
9. connection_type: strings per size (same for both types).
10. length_mm: lists per size.
11. body_material: brass (GKMV40 models), composite (GKMV40P models).

For values entries: {model, value, footnote_markers} — no unit per value; unit at attribute level. Schema example shows values entries without unit. OK.

Do I include q3/q1 etc at type_level? Yes: ratio_q3_q1: 400, ratio_q2_q1: 1.6, ratio_q3_q4: 1.25.

MPE entries:
- type_level: maximum_permissible_error_lower_flowrate_zone: value {min:-5, max:5}? Hmm, I said earlier maybe just 5. Let me think: "±5 %" → the error limit. Using {min:-5,max:5} with unit "%" is a fair structured representation. I'll do that.
- config_level for upper zone:
  attribute: "maximum_permissible_error_upper_flowrate_zone", axis: "water_temperature", values: [{condition: "≤ 30 °C", value: {min:-2,max:2}, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "> 30 °C", value: {min:-3,max:3}, unit_symbol: "%"}]

Wait the config_level values shape: "{condition, value}" per rule 5; "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". OK.

Type-level other characteristics:

- temperature_class: {value: "T30 or T50"} — structured values must be objects with value/unit_symbol/unit_id/footnote_markers. For string values, unit null.
- water_pressure_class: {value: "MAP 16"}
- pressure_loss_class: {value: "ΔP 63"}
- environmental_class: {value: "B, O", footnote_markers: ["1)"]}
- electromagnetic_environment: {value: "E1", footnote_markers: ["1)"]}
- mechanical_class: {value: "M1", footnote_markers: ["1)"]}

- minimum_straight_length_outlet_pipe: {value: 0, unit_symbol: "mm"}

- reed_sensor_max_voltage: {value: 48, unit_symbol: "V", footnote_markers:["2)"]} plus reed_sensor_voltage_type {value:"DC/AC"}; reed_sensor_max_current: {value: 50, unit_symbol: "mA", footnote_markers:["2)"]}
- inductive_sensor_max_voltage: {value: 24, unit_symbol: "V", footnote_markers:["2)"]}; inductive_sensor_voltage_type: {value:"DC"}; inductive_sensor_max_current: {value: 20, unit_symbol: "mA", footnote_markers:["2)"]}

measuring_principle: {value: "positive displacement"}
accuracy_class: {value: 2}

Marking info: skip or include as description.

Now units: "m³/h" — use unit_symbol "m³/h". unit_id null. Fine.

Values format check: q values like "0.0100" → 0.01 numeric. "0.0063" → 0.0063.

Lengths as lists: [110,115,134,165,190] — arrays of numbers are okay as value lists (not ranges). For model_level values, I'll put array for length per model. The structured form says value: number | {min,max} | string. A list of discrete values... rule 2 says lists of values for the SAME attribute across models → model matrix. But here multiple lengths per single model. Options: string "110; 115; 134; 165; 190" or array. I'll use arrays of numbers — pragmatic. Hmm, strict schema: value: <number | {min,max} | string>. Arrays deviate. But matrix_tables rows are free-form objects. For model_level, maybe safer to keep lengths only in matrix_table rows, and in model_level use a string "110; 115; 134; 165; 190"? Strings are allowed. But numbers are preferred... The lengths are genuinely multiple variants. I'll put them in matrix_table "Installation details by nominal diameter" with length arrays, and ALSO include model_level entry with arrays? Deviating from schema might break parsers. Let me use string representation "110; 115; 134; 165; 190"? Or omit from model_level and keep in matrix table. I think keeping in matrix table is cleanest, and also include in model_level as array — risky. 

Decision: include lengths in matrix_tables (rows with arrays) and in model_level as array values. Actually let me reconsider: the instruction "Don't fabricate" but arrays aren't fabrication. Many implementations would handle it. However strictness suggests value must be number|range|string. A set of discrete lengths could be represented as a string listing. I'll use arrays in matrix_tables only, and for model_level I'll include "length" attribute with array values — hmm.

Alternative: create model_level attribute "length" with value as string "110; 115; 134; 165; 190". That's allowed (string). But then numbers lost. The matrix table preserves numeric arrays. I'll do: model_level lengths omitted; matrix_tables include them. Hmm, but model-level completeness... The matrix table covers it. OK: lengths only in matrix_tables. Similarly connection_type only in matrix_tables? Connection type is a string; could be model_level too. I'll put connection_type in matrix table as arrays of strings, and skip in model_level to avoid duplication. Actually model_level example in R137 included qmax etc. only for the numeric flow columns. I'll follow: model_level gets numeric per-model attributes (q1-q4, indicating range, resolutions, rapid testing resolution, nominal diameter). Installation details (connection, lengths) go to matrix table.

indicating_range for DN15: "9999 or 99 999" → string "9999 or 99 999". Keep as string. For others: 99999 number.

resolution "0.000002 or 0.00002" string for DN15; 0.00002 for others.

Now components: I'll include:
{
  "role": "ancillary device",
  "type_designations": ["reed impulse transmitter (reed sensor)", "inductive transmitter (inductive sensor)"],
  "alternatives": "OR",
  "characteristics": {
    "reed_sensor": {"maximum_voltage": {...}, ...}
  }
}
Hmm, the characteristics{} for components is free-form. Maybe simpler: two components entries? They're alternatives — one entry with alternatives OR. Sub-characteristics: for reed: u_max 48 V DC/AC, i_max 50 mA; for inductive: 24 V DC, 20 mA. I'll structure characteristics as {"reed_sensor": {...}, "inductive_sensor": {...}}. That's fine as free-form.

Also note footnote 2 applies: not tested. Add "test_status": "not tested".

test_reports dates: convert to ISO: 2023-08-10, 2023-08-09, 2022-09-27, 2021-10-22, 2021-11-30. Pages: 33, 26, 29, 90, 67. Note "33 pages including annex 1" → pages: 33.

Documentation file: {id: "0511-UL-V041-23", role: "documentation_file"} — schema test_reports[] includes role documentation_file. I'll add it to test_reports with role documentation_file, or as separate? Schema: test_reports[]: id, date, pages, role. documentation_file is one of the roles. Add {id: "0511-UL-V041-23", role: "documentation_file"}.

Which is right? Page 1 has explicit "Person responsible: Jan Kalandra". Page 2 "The OIML Issuing Authority: RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body". Hmm. The schema allows one. I'll use Jan Kalandra (explicit label) and add person_title omitted. But then Klenovský lost. Maybe add both? Fields are single-valued. I'll go with Pavel Klenovský since he signs as the issuing authority... Actually "Person responsible" is the explicit field the schema describes. Hmm. Many CMI certs list Jan Kalandra as contact person. The signature block is the issuing authority representative. I'll include person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra" per the label, and note Klenovský in... there's no field. Alternatively person_responsible: "RNDr. Pavel Klenovský", person_title: "Head of Certification Body". 

I think the signature block is more authoritative for the certificate issuance. But rule: "Person responsible: Jan Kalandra" is literally the person responsible field. I'll use Jan Kalandra. No title given for him, so omit title. Hmm, but then we lose Klenovský entirely. The schema is what it is. Actually — maybe I can set person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra" and person_title: null... Let me just do that. Or should I? Consider typical extraction: page 1 lists "Person responsible". That maps directly. Go with it.
